gen-gf-gabarito-fs-nunito: Expressive from the first glance, Gabarito cuts its terminals open so the counters seem to flow outward. Nunito sits beside it with rounder, taller lowercase bowls, friendly and easygoing next to that single-nib energy.
gen-gf-gabarito-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Gabarito draws each letter as if with one nib, its terminals sliced open and its look unmistakably distinctive. Pilcrow Rounded follows in warm, tall lowercase with curves that refuse to close, so making the heading small would waste its personality.
gen-gf-gabarito-fs-quicksand: Terminals cut open so the counters flow outward give Gabarito a one-nib, hand-drawn look that is hard to mistake. Quicksand takes over below with tall, bulb-round lowercase and bars of identical thickness, so a larger size would suit that body well.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-akatab: Gabarito forms every glyph from a ribbon of constant width, with open-cut terminals and a distinctive hand. Akatab answers with round, cupped letters in a lower, quieter sans, and a heading shrunk too small would lose that ribbon.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-alan-sans: Curves as heavy as the stems, like cord, make Gabarito instantly recognizable, with terminals cut open to let the counters flow outward. Alan Sans keeps its curve tails held well back and its voice low and modern, so one grabs attention while the other simply informs.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-albert-sans: Albert Sans reads as a plain sans with apertures that stay open at tiny sizes and strokes that hold their thickness in every direction. Gabarito sits above it with expressive, open-cut terminals, giving the page a lively head and a steady body.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-alef: Pipe-cleaner letters with a hand-drawn feel, cut open at the terminals so the counters flow outward, define Gabarito. Alef keeps to open-ended curves in a quiet, clean sans, which makes their contrast the pair's best quality.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-alegreya-sans-sc: A steady, unvarying line weight and open-cut terminals give Gabarito a distinctive, expressive hand all its own. And Alegreya Sans SC, a plain sans with a welcoming gap in the c, carries a longer stretch of text smoothly and without fuss.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-almarai: Loose, one-nib drawing and terminals cut open so the counters flow outward make Gabarito feel expressive. Almarai takes the lower register in a plain sans whose line width never swells or tapers, so its letters never seem to pinch shut.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-amarna: Expressive Gabarito draws with a single-nib look, its terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. And Amarna, a plain sans with contrast-free strokes and unclogged small counters, keeps a longer stretch of text clean and easy to follow.
